slides.say: Two congruent circles, with centers O and P, have a radius of six centimeters, and they intersect at A and B. The minor arc A B is one quarter of the circumference of each circle. What is the area of the union of the two circles?

The union is everything that is inside at least one of the circles, the whole grey shape. It's a shaded-area question. But no single familiar shape around it is given, so we can't take one big area and subtract a piece. [short pause] We'll solve it in two different ways, by cutting it into pieces we know, and by taking away the overlap. Then we'll see what estimating can do.

Let's start with the math way. In a case like this, we go to the givens and see what we can get out of them. The minor arc A B is a quarter of the circumference of circle O. A quarter of the circle means a central angle of a quarter of three hundred sixty, ninety degrees.
at: The minor arc A B is a quarter

slides.say: But no central angle is drawn, so we draw one. A radius from O to A, and a radius from O to B. The angle between them is ninety degrees, and each radius is six.
at: A radius from O to A

slides.say: The same in circle P. The circles are congruent, so P A and P B are also six, and the angle at P is also ninety.
Now look at O A P B. All four sides are six, so it's at least a rhombus. And its angle at O is ninety degrees. A rhombus with a right angle is a square, so O A P B is a square.
at: Now look at O A P B

slides.say: [short pause] Here's the figure again, with the square. Now I see how to find the grey area. It cuts into three pieces we know, with no overlap. The left three-quarter circle, the square, and the right three-quarter circle. Some people call each three-quarter circle a Pac-Man. It's a circle without its quarter.
One whole circle is pi r squared, pi times six squared, thirty-six pi. A quarter of thirty-six pi is nine pi. So three quarters is three times nine pi, twenty-seven pi.
The square is six squared, thirty-six. So the union is twenty-seven pi, plus thirty-six, plus twenty-seven pi, which is fifty-four pi plus thirty-six. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now a second way, the math way again, this time by taking away the overlap. Take the two whole circles. Each one is thirty-six pi, so together they're seventy-two pi.
But the middle part, where the circles overlap, is inside both circles. So we counted it twice, and we must take it away once.
How big is the overlap? The chord A B cuts it into two equal pieces. Look at the right piece, in circle O. It's the quarter circle A O B, minus the triangle A O B.
at: minus the triangle A O B

slides.say: The quarter circle is a quarter of thirty-six pi, nine pi. The triangle has two legs of six and a right angle, so its area is six times six over two, eighteen.
at: The quarter circle is a quarter

slides.say: So one piece is nine pi minus eighteen. The overlap is two of these pieces, so we double the whole difference. That's eighteen pi minus thirty-six.

Now take the whole overlap away from seventy-two pi. Seventy-two pi minus the overlap, eighteen pi minus thirty-six. The minus before the overlap turns minus thirty-six into plus thirty-six. So it's seventy-two pi minus eighteen pi, plus thirty-six. That's fifty-four pi plus thirty-six, choice number three again.
[pause] Now let's estimate. It's hard to finish this way, but it's easy to rule out two choices. The left circle alone is thirty-six pi.

And the grey shape has more than that. O P is the diagonal of the square, so it's longer than the side, six. Every point of the right half of circle P is at least that far from O. So that half is outside circle O.
at: the right half of circle P

slides.say: It adds eighteen pi, and the middle piece between them adds a bit more. So the union is more than thirty-six pi plus eighteen pi, fifty-four pi.
at: So the union is more than

slides.say: We need more than fifty-four pi. Now compare twenty-seven pi with thirty-six. Pi is more than three, so twenty-seven pi is more than eighty-one, much more than thirty-six. So twenty-seven pi plus thirty-six is less than twenty-seven pi plus twenty-seven pi, which is fifty-four pi. Twenty-seven pi plus eighteen is even smaller. So choice numbers one and four are out.
at: So twenty-seven pi plus thirty-six is less
